title: A table, a cubic and an inverse

stimulus.title: Values of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>, and the function <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>
stimulus.html:
The table gives values of the function ff at selected inputs. The function gg is defined by g(x)=0.5x3−2x+1g(x) = 0.5x^3 - 2x + 1 for every real number xx.
Values of the function f at x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4
xx-2-101234
f(x)f(x)52-13620

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find the value of f(g(2))f(g(2)), or indicate that it cannot be found from the information given. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: The inner value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2) = 1</annotation></semantics></math> shown, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(2)) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.5(8) - 4 + 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(2)) = f(1) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(2)) = f(1) = 3</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2) = 1</annotation></semantics></math> computed

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.5(2)^3 - 2(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4 - 4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(2)) = f(1) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find every value of xx in the table for which f(x)=2f(x) = 2.

rubric.point: Both <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, and no other value
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(-1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(3) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: From the table, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(-1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(3) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find every value of xx for which g(x)=2g(x) = 2. Give each answer correct to three decimal places.

rubric.point: All three solutions, each correct to three decimal places
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.675</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx -1.675</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.539</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx -0.539</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.214</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 2.214</annotation></semantics></math>
values that round or truncate to these three

parts.sample: Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 0.5x^3 - 2x + 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2</annotation></semantics></math> on a window such as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4 \le x \le 4</annotation></semantics></math>; they meet three times: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.675</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx -1.675</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.539</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx -0.539</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.214</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 2.214</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Write the end behavior of gg as xx decreases without bound, using limit notation.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} g(x) = -\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, in correct limit notation
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} g(x) = -\infty</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} (0.5x^3 - 2x + 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\infty</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The leading term <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5x^3</annotation></semantics></math> is negative and grows without bound in size as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> decreases, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} g(x) = -\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is ff invertible? Give a reason for your answer using values from the table.

rubric.point: No, with two specific inputs that share an output
accept: No, because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(-1) = f(3) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

No: the inputs <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> both give the output <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: No. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(-1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(3) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: two different inputs give the same output, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> has no inverse.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Is gg invertible on the set of real numbers? Give a reason for your answer using specific values of gg.

rubric.point: No, with two specific inputs of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> that share an output
accept: No, because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(0) = g(2) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>

No, because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> takes the value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> at three inputs (part B(i))

parts.sample: No. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(0) = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.5(8) - 4 + 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so two different inputs give the same output and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> has no inverse on the real numbers.
